newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index dips at noon led by property.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index dips at noon led by property.

text.p: Declines in property stocks drove Shenzhen's B share index down slightly at midday on Monday, with caution prevailing in the remaining days of the annual results reporting season, brokers said.
The foreign currency B index shed 0.65 points or 0.37 percent to 175.98 points on turnover of HK$79.8 million.
Steep declines in the property sector, led by Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Real Estate & Properties (Group) Co Ltd, weighed on the market, said an analyst at China Guotai Securities.
The property firm was the worst performer on the B share market this morning after it announced poor 1996 results.
Its shares dived HK$0.45 or 9.96 percent to HK$4.07 on volume of 358,600 shares.
The company announced at the weekend a net loss of 26.34 million yuan for 1996 based on international accounting standards.
Based on Chinese standards, the company posted a net profit of 1.7 million yuan for 1996, down 99.56 percent from 392.41 million yuan in 1995.
"SEZ's results stunned investors and sparked heavy selling in other property firms which have yet to release their 1996 results," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities Co said.
"The stock is going to continue to decline sharply in later sessions as earnings were far worse than expected," the J&A analyst said.
Property firm Hainan Pearl River plunged HK$0.29 or 8.95 percent to HK$2.95.
"But market sentiment remains positive after a correction that lasted for several sessions," the Guotai analyst said, adding the index was seeking support around the 175-point level.
The A share index gained 5.76 points or 1.19 percent to 489.61. Turnover was a heavy 8.53 billion yuan, compared with 17.8 billion yuan for the whole of Friday.
SEZ Real Estate was also among the biggest losers in the A share market, tumbling 1.29 yuan or 9.98 percent to 11.64 yuan.
